# @arkite-ui/core v0.21.1

> React components for multi-tenant SaaS admin panels. Tailwind CSS v4 +
> Radix UI + TypeScript. Pure UI only: no business logic, auth, stores, or
> routing — data comes in via props, events go out via callbacks.
>
> Arkite UI is an open-source project by Foson (https://foson.co), a Taiwan-based
> software company. Docs: https://ui.foson.co · Repo: https://github.com/foson-co/arkite-ui
> Not affiliated with Arkite NV (arkite.com, industrial operator guidance).

## Setup

```bash
pnpm add @arkite-ui/core
# peer deps: react react-dom tailwindcss zustand lucide-react
# optional:  framer-motion (Animated* variants)
```

```css
/* app.css — Tailwind v4, tokens included */
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "@arkite-ui/core/styles.css";
```

## Rules for generated code

1. Import UI from `@arkite-ui/core` — never rebuild primitives that exist (see inventory below).
2. Use semantic token utilities only (`bg-card`, `text-muted-foreground`, `border-border`) — never raw palette classes (`bg-red-50`), never `dark:` color overrides (tokens handle dark mode), never arbitrary values (`text-[13px]`).
3. Components follow the controlled/uncontrolled React convention: `value`+`onChange` controls, `defaultValue` doesn't.
4. Keep API calls, routes, and business models in the app layer.
5. Building a whole page? Match it against the recipes below **before** assembling one
   from scratch, then **install it instead of writing it**: `npx arkite-ui add <recipe>`
   writes the tested composition into the project (`--out`, `--name`, `--force`), leaving
   you only the sample data and API calls to replace. Generating the wiring by hand is
   the step that introduces bugs the recipe already solved.

Full design rules (color/spacing/typography/layout recipes): DESIGN.md, shipped
inside this package — also embedded in llms-full.txt.

## Core patterns

### Server-paginated table

`useServerTable` owns the six controlled props server mode needs; you supply
`data` + `totalRows` and fetch on `queryKey`:

```tsx
import { DataTable, useServerTable, type Column } from '@arkite-ui/core'

const table = useServerTable({ initialPageSize: 20 })
const [page, setPage] = useState({ items: [], total: 0 })
useEffect(() => {
  fetchUsers(table.query).then(setPage) // query = { page, pageSize, sort, filters }
}, [table.queryKey])

<DataTable columns={columns} data={page.items} totalRows={page.total}
  getRowKey={(r) => r.id} {...table.props} />
```

Client-side tables need none of that: pass `data` and the table filters,
sorts, and paginates itself.

### Toasts

```tsx
import { useToast, ToastContainer } from '@arkite-ui/core'

// once, near the app root:
<ToastContainer position="bottom-right" />

const toast = useToast()
toast.success('Saved', { description: 'Changes are live.' })

// error handling in catch blocks — wire the app's parser once at startup:
toast.configure({ formatError: getErrorMessage })
// then every call site is one line (title = prefix, description = parsed message):
catch (err) { toast.fromError(err, { prefix: 'Failed to save' }) }
```

### Theming

```tsx
import { createTheme, applyTheme } from '@arkite-ui/core'
applyTheme(createTheme({ primary: '#7c3aed' })) // HSL tokens from one hex
```

A project's brand belongs in a committed `arkite.theme.json`
(`{ name, primary, accent, radius }`) rather than hand-copied CSS variables.
Generate the CSS from it with `npx arkite-ui theme apply`, or in-process via
`themeFileToCSS(parseThemeFile(json))` from `@arkite-ui/core/theme` — a server-safe
entry that loads no components. `parseThemeFile` rejects malformed hex and
unknown keys, which `createTheme` alone would pass through as `NaN` tokens.

## Recipes — page-level compositions

Whole pages assembled from the library, each one rendered and tested in CI.
Machine-readable index: registry.json (ships in the package).
Install one with `npx arkite-ui add <name>` — do not retype it.

### crud-list-page — CRUD List Page

Search + filters over a sortable, selectable, paginated table, with bulk actions and a guarded destructive path.
- Use when: A list page whose rows are already in memory and the page needs filtering, sorting, multi-select, bulk actions, or a delete confirmation.
- Not when: The server does the filtering/sorting/slicing — use `server-side-table`. A read-only handful of rows with no interaction — use `Table` directly, no recipe needed.
- Composes: Badge, BulkActionBar, Button, DataTable, DeleteConfirmDialog, FilterBar, FilterBarActions, FilterBarFilters, FilterBarSearch, FilterSelect, PageHeader, ToastContainer, toast
- Source (ships in the package, copy it): src/stories/recipes/CrudListPage.demo.tsx — docs: https://ui.foson.co/?path=/docs/recipes-crud-list-page--docs

### server-side-table — Server-Side Table

A table whose sorting and pagination round-trip to the server: the page owns the query state, the API returns one slice plus a total.
- Use when: The API returns one pre-sorted page plus a total count, so the table can never know the full ordering — sorting and pagination must be controlled.
- Not when: All rows fit in memory — leave the table uncontrolled and use `crud-list-page`.
- Composes: Badge, DataTable, PageHeader, useServerTable
- Source (ships in the package, copy it): src/stories/recipes/ServerSideTable.demo.tsx — docs: https://ui.foson.co/?path=/docs/recipes-server-side-table--docs

### dashboard-page — Dashboard

A KPI row over compact widget cards — sparkline trends and a recent-activity table in one responsive grid.
- Use when: An overview page that answers 'is everything okay?' at a glance and links out for detail.
- Not when: The page IS the detail view, or the numbers need drill-down in place — build a list or detail page instead. Full charting belongs in a dedicated chart library, not `Sparkline`.
- Composes: Badge, Card, CardContent, CardHeader, DataTable, PageHeader, Sparkline, StatCard, StatGroup
- Source (ships in the package, copy it): src/stories/recipes/DashboardPage.demo.tsx — docs: https://ui.foson.co/?path=/docs/recipes-dashboard--docs

### detail-drawer-page — Detail + Drawer Edit

A record's read view with an edit drawer, a dirty-close guard, and a confirmed destructive action.
- Use when: Editing a record while the user still needs the record on screen for reference.
- Not when: The edit should interrupt and take over (short one-shot forms, confirmations) — use `Modal`. A full create/edit page with many sections — use `form-page`.
- Composes: Badge, Button, Card, ConfirmDialog, DescriptionItem, DescriptionList, Drawer, Form, FormActions, FormControl, FormField, FormLabel, FormMessage, Input, PageHeader, Textarea, ToastContainer, toast
- Source (ships in the package, copy it): src/stories/recipes/DetailDrawerPage.demo.tsx — docs: https://ui.foson.co/?path=/docs/recipes-detail-drawer-edit--docs

### form-page — Form Page

A sectioned create/edit page: grouped fields, mixed control types, submit-time validation, and a guarded submit.
- Use when: A create or edit page big enough to need sections, help text, and inline validation messages.
- Not when: The form is short enough to live in a drawer next to a read view — use `detail-drawer-page`.
- Composes: Button, Form, FormActions, FormControl, FormDescription, FormField, FormLabel, FormMessage, FormSection, Input, PageHeader, Select, Switch, Textarea, ToastContainer, toast
- Source (ships in the package, copy it): src/stories/recipes/FormPage.demo.tsx — docs: https://ui.foson.co/?path=/docs/recipes-form-page--docs

### tenant-admin-shell — Tenant Admin Shell

The app frame: localized AdminLayout with permission-aware navigation, the signed-in user, and a tenant switcher.
- Use when: Starting a multi-tenant admin app — this is the outermost shell every page renders inside.
- Not when: A single-tenant app with no tenant scope — use `AdminLayout` without `TenantSwitcher`.
- Composes: AdminLayout, Card, CardContent, CardHeader, DescriptionItem, DescriptionList, LocaleProvider, SegmentedControl, TenantSwitcher, toast, zhTW
- Source (ships in the package, copy it): src/stories/recipes/TenantAdminShell.demo.tsx — docs: https://ui.foson.co/?path=/docs/recipes-tenant-admin-shell--docs
